subject: Mental Models
title: Connecting Disciplines
description: A short lesson to help you apply Connecting Disciplines.

hook.text: Darwin studied barnacles, geology, and economics before writing On the Origin of Species. All three fed his theory.

buildup.text: He borrowed Malthus's population model from economics and applied it to biology. Cross-pollination worked.

discovery.text: Breakthroughs often come from importing a model from one field into another where nobody thought to look.

twist.text: Specialists go deep but stay narrow. Generalists go wide but stay shallow. The edge is doing both.

climax.text: Mental models are the bridges between disciplines. They let a biologist think like an economist and vice versa.

punchline.text: The best ideas cross borders. Models are the passport.

quiz.question: How did Darwin's study of economics help his biology theory?
options: He borrowed Malthus's population model for natural selection
Economics taught him to write better
